content.text:
I did a manual sweep of every page under `src/app/footy/**` and the components they render (forms, tables, D3/SVG charts, grid layouts), looking for the same class of bug you'd already fixed in `GameDaySummary`/`GameResultForm` — content that's sized/laid out in a way that doesn't reflow when the effective viewport shrinks (which is exactly what browser zoom does).

**Confirmed bug: Country Map page (`/footy/countrymap`, `PlayerCountryMap.tsx`)**

The SVG world map is rendered with hard-coded pixel attributes:

```tsx
<svg ref={svgRef} width={width} height={height} />   // defaults: width=960, height=500
```

There's no `viewBox`, no CSS (`max-width: 100%`/`height: auto`), and no `ResizeObserver` resizing it. Every other D3 chart in the codebase (`FamilyTree`, `PieChart`, `MoneyChart`, `PlayerHeatmap`) measures its container and redraws responsively — this one doesn't. At high zoom (or any narrow effective viewport), the 960px-wide map just overflows the `Paper` and the page, forcing horizontal scroll with no fallback, since nothing in the layout constrains or scrolls it.

Everything else I checked already follows the responsive patterns you'd expect and should be fine under zoom:
- Forms/tables using `Group`/`Flex` with `wrap="wrap"` or responsive `direction={{ base: ..., ... }}` (admin dashboard, winners/tables pages, ResponsesForm, GameDayList, etc.)
- Wide admin tables (`AdminPlayerList`, `AdminUserList`, `PickerForm`, `DrinkersForm`) are correctly wrapped in `Table.ScrollContainer`
- `PlayerProfile`'s card grid uses container queries (`type="container"` + em breakpoints), which scale correctly with zoom
- The other D3 visualisations (`FamilyTree`, `PieChart`, `MoneyChart`, `PlayerHeatmap`) all use `ResizeObserver` to stay responsive

One minor, lower-priority item: `Turnout.tsx`'s stats table (`maw="24rem"`, `layout="fixed"`, no `Table.ScrollContainer`) is the only data table without a scroll fallback like its siblings have — low risk since it's narrow and rem-based, but worth a defensive `Table.ScrollContainer` wrap for consistency if you want belt-and-braces.

Want me to fix the `PlayerCountryMap` SVG (switch to `viewBox` + CSS scaling, matching the responsive pattern the other charts use)?
Turnout is fine. Fix PlayerCountryMap

I did a second, more targeted pass — including trying to visually verify behaviour at a simulated narrow viewport, though the browser tooling in this session couldn't reliably shrink the effective viewport (window resize didn't propagate to the page, and embedding the site in an iframe was blocked, presumably by CSP). So this finding is from static analysis with the numbers worked through, not a confirmed visual repro like `PlayerCountryMap` was.

**Possible risk: site header (`CustomAppShell.tsx`)**

```tsx
<AppShell header={{ height: 60 }} ...>
  <AppShell.Header>
    <Container>
      <Group justify="space-between" className="px-6">
        <Burger hiddenFrom="sm" ... />
        <Link><Image w={56} h={56} .../></Link>
        <Group gap="xs"><Text>Toastboy FC</Text>{devMode && <Badge>dev mode</Badge>}</Group>
      </Group>
    </Container>
  </AppShell.Header>
```

The header has a **fixed** height (`60`, not a minimum), and the row inside it isn't set to `wrap="nowrap"` — so it relies on Mantine's default `wrap="wrap"`. If the row's content (burger + 56px crest + "Toastboy FC" + the "dev mode" badge) can't fit on one line, it wraps to a second line that has nowhere to go, since the header box won't grow — it'd overlap the page content directly beneath it.

Working through the minimum widths, this only becomes a real problem under fairly extreme zoom (roughly 400%+, i.e. an effective viewport under ~350–400px) — normal zoom levels have comfortable margin. It's more likely to bite with the "dev mode" badge showing (extra ~80px) than in production. I'd call this a plausible edge case worth a defensive fix, not an urgent bug.

**Unrelated thing I noticed in passing**: that `className="px-6"` on the header's `Group` has no effect — this project doesn't have Tailwind configured, so it's dead markup left over from somewhere. Not a zoom issue, just worth cleaning up if you want.

Everything else from this pass (Modals — Mantine's built-in responsive sizing, fine; NavBarNested — no fixed widths; the remaining D3 charts, forms, and grids) checked out clean, consistent with the first pass.

Want me to make the header defensively responsive (e.g. `wrap="nowrap"` with the crest/text allowed to shrink, or drop the badge into the wrapping-safe side) and drop the dead `px-6` class, or would you rather verify the header at real high zoom yourself first before I touch it?
